answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut and 14-day renewal deadline create urgency, but the 94% volume utilization leaves no margin for supply disruption. Switching vendors or adding a second source would introduce onboarding risk and delay under this timeline. Deferring is not viable with hard expiration. Renewing the incumbent at current terms fails the cost mandate. Renegotiating leverages memory_c4 (successful benchmarking recovered margin and improved terms) and memory_c6 (multi-year commitments unlocked volume pricing). Pulling memory_c4 to verify the specific benchmarking approach and what moved the incumbent will inform whether aggressive renegotiation can close the 18% gap or a portion of it. The incumbent relationship is stable (memory_c1) and invoicing is reliable (memory_c2), making them negotiable partners. This preserves the delivery buffer while testing whether the incumbent can meet cost pressure. If renegotiation fails, the next cycle can pivot to switching or dual-sourcing with fuller preparation.
